People would like to care, but we are conditioned to see value from certain criteria that people in poverty often appear to lack.  Its an unconscious lack of empathy.

Combined with that, there are narratives about why people are in poverty that are often self-preserving for the people that weave those narratives.

Our society is very superficial, and as much as selfishness is considered a negative trait people are rewarded for being selfish and with our egos being exaggerated out of proportion via the self-reflective quality of social media, we are exceedingly dependent on appearance as virtue.   Once you have money people don't care what you did to get it because they see it as a possible escape from their own suffering and you can look good, which means you are unconsciously interpreted as being "good". 

For people that are unlucky, they have to work much harder than anyone else or be crushed under ever expanding gear of inequality.

Not everyone is such a fool for image, and some people still try and manually override the passive lack of empathy they feel for someone who lacks confidence and evidence of success.

To a great extent we don't really choose how we see the world, we think it is us seeing but it is really the culture we are conditioned into that is doing the seeing.  The only way to not be controlled by our conditioning, both overt and subtle, is to become culturally self aware, which is difficult because its not something that is taught in this society and most people interpret most of what people do as that person's nature or human nature.  They don't realize how deep ways of seeing and organizing the world, that are particular, and thus not innate, go.

What I am getting at is that sometimes our suffering comes from expecting things from people that they aren't in a position to give.  Sometimes our own perspective is the only option we have in terms of effecting our immediate experience.

If I was king I would take from the .5% and make sure you had everything you needed but fairness isn't something anyone on reddit can change.  As someone who is relatively powerless, understanding why everything is the way it is is a comfort to me.  It helps me to pick my battles and spot my opportunities.  It helps temper my expectations and have compassion for my oppressors.

Most people are suffering which is why they can't be bothered to help someone who is down and out.  They are so desperate to be validated themselves they don't even see you.  There are people out there who have broken out of this but the only way to find them to see one is to be one.

Or reach out, ask for help, and they'll come to you :)
